name: Medley Town Council

meetings.pattern: First Monday of every month, 7:00 p.m., Council Chambers at the Medley Municipal Services Facility, 7777 NW 72nd Avenue, Medley, FL 33166. If the Monday is a legal holiday, the meeting moves to the following Tuesday.

schedule.note: Regular meeting by the first-Monday rule. The October 5, 2026 agenda carried item 13A.9, 'Discussion and Action on the Cancellation of the November 2, 2026 Regular Council Meeting'; check with the clerk whether it was cancelled.
Regular meeting by the first-Monday rule on the council meetings page; no agenda posted yet.

phases.name: Budget workshop on the proposed budget and tentative millage
phases.decides: Council discusses the manager's proposed FY 2026-27 budget and the tentative millage based on the certified taxable value; special meeting 6:00 p.m. at the Municipal Services Facility.

phases.name: First budget hearing (tentative millage and budget, first reading)
phases.decides: Proposed tentative millage rate by resolution, tentative budget, and first reading of the budget ordinance for October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027; Thursday 6:00 p.m.

phases.name: Second budget hearing (final millage and budget)
phases.decides: Final millage and adoption of the FY 2026-27 budget ordinance. Date is from the October 5, 2026 agenda, which approves minutes of the 'Special Council Meeting of September 22, 2026 - 2nd Budget'; the notice itself was not posted on the town's 2026 notices page.

phases.name: Fiscal year begins
phases.decides: Budget and millage take effect for October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027.

phases.name: Town general election
phases.decides: Two council member seats (vote for up to two) among Edgar Ayala, Gloria Hernandez, Ivan Pacheco, Lizelh Rodriguez and Juan Stefano; polls 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

levers.how: Speak during the Public Comment item at the regular meeting in the Council Chambers. Budget hearing notices say all interested parties may attend and be heard.
levers.rules: Each speaker's comments are limited to three minutes (agenda notice). Decorum rules on the agenda: no insulting or slanderous remarks, no clapping, heckling or signs; the mayor may bar a disruptive speaker unless a majority of the council votes otherwise. No sign-up procedure is printed on the agenda. The town does not provide translation.

levers.how: No written comment procedure is published. Email the Town Clerk, Victoria Martinez, at vmartinez@townofmedley.com or townclerk@townofmedley.com and ask that it be shared with the council.
Email the mayor or any council member directly (lstefano, ajinete, eayala, lrodriguez, Lourdes.rodriguez at townofmedley.com) or call Town Hall at 305-887-9541.
levers.rules: Town Hall hours Monday to Wednesday 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., Thursday 7 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed Friday.

levers.how: Call 305-887-9541 or email townclerk@townofmedley.com; the clerk is the records custodian. Many records are in the Laserfiche public library at medleydocs.com.

Charter amendment by petition is available under state law: a petition signed by 10 percent of the registered electors as of the last municipal general election forces a referendum at the next general election or a special election.
levers.rules: Fla. Stat. 166.031(1). The town charter's own initiative section, if any, could not be read: the municode library and the town's municipal code page both returned errors to automated fetching.

levers.how: Not found. The charter was not readable (see petition); only the state charter-amendment referendum route under Fla. Stat. 166.031 is confirmed.

Recall follows Florida's uniform municipal recall statute, which applies to every city whether or not its charter has a recall section. For a town with fewer than 500 registered electors the first petition needs the greater of 50 electors or 10 percent, gathered within 30 days; for 500 to 1,999 electors, the greater of 100 or 10 percent. A second 'Recall Petition and Defense' round needs 15 percent within 60 days.
levers.rules: Fla. Stat. 100.361(1), (2)(b), (2)(f), (3)(a), (3)(c), (11), (12). File with the Town Clerk. Medley's elector count was not checked; pick the tier from the county's registration figures.
levers.deadline: 30 days for the first round; 60 days for the second

levers.how: The Town Clerk is the municipal Supervisor of Elections; candidate filings go to the clerk's office at 7777 NW 72nd Avenue. The 2026 qualifying dates were not posted on any fetchable town page.
levers.rules: Nonpartisan. Elections are run under Title IX, Florida Statutes (chapters 97-106).

levers.how: Vote for up to two council members on November 3, 2026, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., at the county-run polling place for Medley precincts.
levers.rules: Registered voters living in the town.

levers.how: No advisory board application page was found; the town's public meetings besides the council are the Code Compliance Special Magistrate hearings.

elections.terms: Mayor and four council members, four-year staggered terms, nonpartisan; municipal elections every two years in November. 2026: two council seats. The mayor and the other two seats were last elected November 2024.

contacts.name: Victoria Martinez, FRP, CMC, Town Clerk

notes: Checked 2026-10-22. Agenda lead time is not stated anywhere found. The second budget hearing date (Sep 22, 2026) is inferred from the Oct 5 agenda's minutes item, not from a notice. Charter: not read; municode.com and the town's municipal code page both failed, so initiative, referendum and recall charter sections and the qualifying period are missing. Recall and petition levers use state statutes. The town's 2026 election notice (with qualifying dates) was not on the 2026 notices page; only the sample ballot was. Public comment rule (three minutes) is from the printed agenda notice. Minutes live in the Laserfiche portal at medleydocs.com, which requires cookies and could not be browsed; legal notices are at medley.realpublicnotices.com, which blocks automated fetching.
